source_usage_contracts.authored_summary: After generating C# or Java, replace the mapping parameter objects at the Run/run call in the generated console or Java GUI host. The page describes one argument per static source/input plus a final output argument; dynamically processed file components do not appear as these arguments.

The ConvertProducts example substitutes string input and a string-writer destination for file-backed XML and reads the writer after mapping. Example calls include StreamInput.createInput and Close/close; they do not supply complete declarations for those members. No example implementation or XML payload is reproduced.
Binary streams and reader/writer objects are expected to be open and ready before the mapping call.

The documented default is to close the stream when run finishes. The C# example assigns false to CloseObjectsAfterRun; the Java example calls setCloseObjectsAfterRun(false). These are usage fragments, not full member declarations.
Java StringOutput takes no constructor argument; getString() retrieves the produced content. The example subsequently calls toString(), but does not declare getString's return type.
C# StringOutput takes a pre-existing StringBuilder; output appends to any data already in it. The example reads the supplied builder afterward.
The later string-output examples still read Products.xml and require it in the working directory; this is distinct from the earlier string-input replacement example.
DocumentOutput requires an empty supplied document; after run that document contains the output and can be manipulated. No ownership or copying guarantee beyond this usage statement is declared.

unresolved_contracts.question: The literal manual signature remains StreamOutput(String filename). The release-bound ConvertProducts source bundle separately exposes an OutputStream constructor; see artifact-observations.json. That does not by itself settle the documentation discrepancy or runtime contract.

The prose describes an inner-exception pointer and NULL absence, but the table says std::exception inner(). Pointer/reference/value return, lifetime, ownership and actual absence representation remain unresolved.
SourceInstanceUnvailableException and java.lang.IllegalArgumentsException are literal source spellings, not silently corrected aliases. Their correspondence to installed declarations is unknown.
The C# host is MappingConsole.cs, but the renamed-host example says MyAppConsole.js. The inconsistency is retained rather than treated as a new supported language or corrected filename.
The prose describes static source/input parameters and a final output parameter, not a complete overload family or multi-target/error contract.

Only twenty displayed constructors and four base names are enumerated. Other constructors, factory declarations, return types, visibility, null validation, encoding/BOM rules, buffering, failure behavior and close-on-error semantics are not exhaustively specified. No such overloads or contracts are inferred.

Exception constructors, full member lists, exact throw sites, payloads and versioned ABI remain unspecified. Unqualified Exception bases are retained without silently qualifying them. The C++ shared methods are not transferred to C# or Java.

The copied application tree and four ConvertProducts inputs now match official 2026r2 installer members; C#/Java source generation is observed. Product-wide installation and platform dependency coverage, schema-wrapper bundles and runtime qualification remain incomplete. See artifact-observations.json.
